subject.title: fix(agents): run-lifecycle reliability — bounded release, evidence-based liveness, watchdog semantics

question: Should PR #102160 land as one atomic stack after soak with the new stale-run, timeout-zero, self-hosted idle, and Codex shared-client recovery defaults?
rationale: The code path appears coherent, but these defaults deliberately change when upgraded gateways release sessions, reclaim stale runs, and retry shared Codex clients.

options.title: Land after soak
options.body: Keep the atomic stack together, finish production soak plus exact-head validation, then merge with the accepted compatibility behavior.

options.title: Accept now
options.body: Merge before additional soak and explicitly own any upgrade-visible timing or delivery changes discovered after release.

options.title: Pause or split
options.body: Hold the PR and split tracks only if maintainers decide the combined compatibility surface is too broad for one release step.

recommendation.title: Land after soak
recommendation.body: Keep the atomic stack together, finish production soak plus exact-head validation, then merge with the accepted compatibility behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the integration stack and recorded the related maintainer decisions on the track PRs.
